title: Nine Names on the Wall
subtitle: 欺凌与霸凌 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 欺凌与霸凌（生活与学习·校园与安全）
meta: 主题语境：欺凌与霸凌（生活与学习·校园与安全）　|　核心词汇：bully　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bully 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my mother was sent to stop ① a bully she could not name, and she said the naming was the whole of the lesson. The ② bully, meaning the boy and not the behaviour, was nine years older in the story and was faced by whoever came last; a bully, she said, is the only thing in a playground that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ bully in that report had the same excuse, and the ④ bully at the back, meaning the one the master watched and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever stopped properly. A bully, my grandmother said, is nine parts fear and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the fear is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bully was the whole of the problem, meaning the bullying itself and not the boy. The ⑥ bully, meaning the behaviour and not any of that, is the only thing in a school that everybody fears and nobody questions; a bully, he said, is either someone you stop or the only word that means both a boy and a behaviour. She said the behaviour is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ bully had become a name in a report, and the report had become an argument about the fear. The ⑧ bully of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine names on the wall and eleven years of watching; a bully, she said, is either the one at the back or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ bully I remember is the one at the back, which was recorded in 1979 and is still described as the worst in the county. A ⑩ bully, my grandmother said in 1984, is the only thing that improves by being named; every bully, she said, is a behaviour that has agreed to look like a boy. She said the behaviour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 恃强凌弱者；霸凌者
B. n. 霸凌者（指那个人本身，与行为相对）
C. 固定搭配：stop a bully 制止一个霸凌者
D. n. 霸凌者（指报告里每一个）
E. n. 霸凌者（指后面那一个）
F. n. 霸凌；欺凌行为（抽象：与那个人相对）
G. n. 那种行为（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bully she could not name
The bully, meaning the boy and not the behaviour
bully was the whole of the problem
the bully had become a name in a report
The bully of the whole thing
A bully, my grandmother said in 1984

answers.why: stop a bully 意为“制止一个霸凌者”，1961 年母亲被派去制止一个她说不出名字的霸凌者。
bully 意为“霸凌者”，指那个人本身而不是行为，故事里大九岁，由最后走的人面对。
bully 指报告里每一个霸凌者，每一个都是同样的借口。
bully 指后面那一个（老师盯着的那个），是唯一有人认真制止过的。
bully 意为“霸凌、欺凌行为”，与那个人相对，父亲说 bully 就是那个问题的全部。
bully 为抽象用法，指那种行为本身，是学校里人人都怕、却没人质疑的东西。
bully 意为“霸凌者”，到 1975 年这个 bully 成了报告里的一个名字。
bully 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是墙上的九个名字和十一年的注视。
bully 意为“霸凌者”，我记得的是后面那一个，1979 年被记录在案，至今仍被说成全县最坏的。
bully 为抽象总称，祖母说霸凌是唯一会因为被点名而变好的东西。
